Request of Councilmember Zernitskaya and Councilmember Zwick that the City Council take a “Support if Amended” position on AB 306 (Shultz) which would impose a six-year moratorium, from June 1, 2025, to June 1, 2031, on the adoption or modification of state and local building standards affecting residential units, with limited exceptions. As noted in the letter from the City of West Hollywood (attached), the City of Santa Monica would request that the bill be amended such that only new residential units would be impacted by the bill. Additionally, the City would request an amendment to clarify that cities and counties may relax local building code standards such that they revert to the state standard, and that state and local governments can adopt the state 2025 code and allow work to begin on the 2031 state building codes before June 1, 2031 in order to proceed with the normal code adoption process for the 2031 code.   CITY OF SANTA MONICA

A regular meeting of the Santa Monica City Council was called to order by Mayor Negrete at 5:30 p.m., on

 CONVENE/PLEDGE  On order of the Mayor, the City Council convened at 5:30 p.m., with all
  members present. Councilmember Snell led the assemblage in the Pledge of
  Allegiance.

 STATEMENT OF  The City of Santa Monica is located on the land of Tovangaar. With
 ACCOUNTABILITY  great respect, the City acknowledges the Gabrieleño/Tongva as the First
 (LAND  People of this ancestral and unceded territory of Kuruvungna, a village
 ACKNOWLEDGEMENT)  that we know as Santa Monica. We honor their elders, past and present,
  and the Gabrieleño descendants who are part of the Gabrieleño /Tongva
  tribes.

  We recognize that these peoples are still here, and as settlers and kuyam
  (guests), we recognize our responsibility and obligation to care for their
  land in partnership with them. The City of Santa Monica commits to
  work in partnership with the Gabrieleño/Tongva people to uplift their
  voices and visibility on their ancestral land.

  The City of Santa Monica Statement of Accountability (Land
  Acknowledgement) was read into the record by Councilmember
  Zernitskaya.

ENTERTAINMENT ZONE
PILOT PROGRAM  Recommended Action
  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Adopt a finding of Categorical Exemption pursuant to Section 15301
  (Existing Facilities) of the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA) Guidelines; and
  2. Introduce and Adopt an Emergency Ordinance Adding Chapter 6.43
  and Amending Section 4.08.200 to the Santa Monica Municipal Code
  Relating to the Entertainment Zone Pilot Program to Promote
  Economic Recovery.

  Questions asked and answered of staff included: have any metrics been
  determined to measure success; has there been any exploration of
  sponsorship opportunities, is the city offering technical assistance to
  businesses; what rationale convinced staff to limit the entertainment zone to
  the 1200 block; what considerations have been made for safety and security
  protocols; has traffic control been discussed with police; what types of
  alcohol will be available in the entertainment zone; what age verification
  methods will be used; how is the city going to make the permitting process
  easier for businesses to participate; was there any attempt to tally what the
  level of costs the city would ask organizers to pay to put on events; is there
  a police substation on the Promenade; are there foot patrols on the
  Promenade; is there anything in SB 969 that prevents allowing open
  containers and consumption of alcohol in approved disposable containers
  during specified entertainment zone hours, rather than only during events;
  why would the city want to do this as a pilot program vs. a permanent
  ordinance; is there potential for the city to hold a design contest for the design
  of the logo on the mandated cup; does the city charge extra fees on top of
  costs for police and fire to event organizers; and will there be ability to
  modify the ordinance in the future.

  Considerable discussion ensued on topics including, but not limited to
  potential for this to lead to economic opportunity and growth; number of
  police needed to secure events; eliminating financial barriers for businesses

  9  April 22, 2025
   to be able to produce events; making this permanent to occur every weekend
  and federal holidays with set hours, including Friday afternoons; extending
  hours to 2:00 a.m. on Sunday for federal holidays that occur on Mondays;
  improving the process map through self-certification or annual insurance
  checks versus event based insurance checks; preference to utilize police
  officers over armed private security; needing to implement a bolder plan for
  the entertainment zone in order to stimulate economic recovery; leveraging
  digital wayfinding kiosks to advertise; including the entire promenade and
  not just the 1200 block; setting regular hours for consistency; making it easy
  to allow vendors to participate and contribute to event costs, but also
  ensuring that the costs imposed by the city are reasonable; not imposing a
  strict requirement that all events are staffed with public safety overtime, but
  rather if an event is large enough to require additional safety precautions,
  there are certain requirements to ensure safety; desire to add more foot
  patrols on the Promenade; potential to also add the area of Santa Monica
  Blvd. between Second and Fourth Street and other opportunities to expand
  this should the Promenade zone do well; activating spaces make them safer;
  people looking for an experience; allowing flexibilities on time based on
  when businesses are in operation.
